---
title: "Indicator family: Health survey indicators, British Columbia"
---

*Status: a published indicator family (milestone M3 in progress). Regenerate
all series with `uv run sohbc build`.*

This page covers the family of British Columbia indicators that the
pipeline extracts from a single Statistics Canada survey table, widening
the project beyond mortality into physical morbidity, mental health,
subjective wellbeing, social wellbeing, and access to care. Each series is
published as its own versioned tidy dataset and trend files; the [life
satisfaction](indicator-life-satisfaction-bc.qmd) series has its own
worked page.

## Provenance

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Domains** | [Physical morbidity, mental health, subjective wellbeing, social wellbeing](../reference/measurement-framework.qmd) |
| **Definition** | Share of British Columbians aged 18 and over reporting each measured characteristic, annual 2015–2024 [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Source** | Statistics Canada, table 13-10-0905-01, *Health indicator statistics, annual estimates* (Canadian Community Health Survey) [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Access** | Statistics Canada Web Data Service (automated full-table download) |
| **Form** | indicator table (published survey summary statistics) |
| **Geography** | British Columbia (no sub-provincial rows in this table) |
| **Coverage** | 2015–2024 (annual); observation window shown on each figure |
| **Frequency / refresh** | annual |
| **Licence** | Statistics Canada Open Licence |
| **Proxy note** | Self-reported proxies, not the state of health itself ([why](../explanation/definition-of-health.qmd#proxies-are-not-the-state-of-health)) |

tAnx = FileAttachment("../data/published/anxiety_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tMood = FileAttachment("../data/published/mood_disorder_bc_trend.json").json()
tDiab = FileAttachment("../data/published/diabetes_bc_trend.json").json()
tBp = FileAttachment("../data/published/high_blood_pressure_bc_trend.json").json()

tSmoke = FileAttachment("../data/published/smoker_daily_bc_trend.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
series = [
  {key: "life_satisfaction_bc", label: "Life satisfaction", domain: "Subjective wellbeing", direction: "higher is better", trend: tLife},
  {key: "perceived_health_fair_poor_bc", label: "Perceived health, fair or poor", domain: "Subjective wellbeing", direction: "lower is better", trend: tPhyH},
  {key: "perceived_mental_health_fair_poor_bc", label: "Perceived mental health, fair or poor", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tMentH},
  {key: "sense_of_belonging_bc", label: "Sense of belonging to local community", domain: "Social wellbeing", direction: "higher is better", trend: tBelong},
  {key: "anxiety_disorder_bc", label: "Anxiety disorder", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tAnx},
  {key: "mood_disorder_bc", label: "Mood disorder", domain: "Mental health", direction: "lower is better", trend: tMood},
  {key: "diabetes_bc", label: "Diabetes", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tDiab},
  {key: "high_blood_pressure_bc", label: "High blood pressure", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tBp},
  {key: "has_regular_provider_bc", label: "Has a regular healthcare provider", domain: "Access to care", direction: "higher is better", trend: tProv},
  {key: "smoker_daily_bc", label: "Current daily smoker", domain: "Physical morbidity", direction: "lower is better", trend: tSmoke}
]
family = series.map(s => {
  const t = s.trend
  const segs = t.segments.length > 1
    ? t.segments.map(g => `${g.slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)} (${g.start}–${g.end})`).join("; ")
    : "single regime"
  return {
    label: s.label,
    domain: s.domain,
    direction: s.direction,
    slope_per_decade: t.overall.slope_per_decade,
    verdict: t.stationarity.verdict,
    change_point: t.change_point ?? "—",
    segments: segs
  }
})
Inputs.table(family, {
  columns: ["label", "domain", "direction", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "change_point", "segments"],
  header: {
    label: "series", domain: "domain", direction: "better if…",
    slope_per_decade: "slope/decade (pp)", verdict: "stationarity",
    change_point: "largest break", segments: "regimes (pp/decade)"
  },
  width: {label: 210, segments: 240}
})
```

    slope_per_decade: t.overall.slope_per_decade,
    verdict: t.stationarity.verdict,
    change_point: cp,
    segments: segs
  }

Inputs.table(family, {
  columns: ["label", "domain", "direction", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "change_point", "segments"],
  header: {
    label: "series", domain: "domain", direction: "better if…",
    slope_per_decade: "slope/decade (pp)", verdict: "stationarity",
    change_point: "largest break", segments: "regimes (pp/decade)"
  },
  width: {label: 210, segments: 240}

```

Each slope is in percentage points per decade over 2015–2024, for both
sexes; a positive slope is not automatically good or bad — the *better
if…* column states the direction that the measurement treats as
favourable. `stationarity` is the pipeline's label from the formal tests
(stationary, nonstationary, or undetermined where the series is too short
for the test to have power); `largest break` is the BIC-selected change
point, where one exists.

## What the family shows

The series are not all moving the same way, and the direction of movement
follows the direction of the measurement:

- **Wellbeing is falling.** Life satisfaction (`-11.5` pp/decade;
  break at 2020) and sense of belonging (`-10.6` pp/decade; break at
  2020) both fell sharply, and both are dated to 2020 by the pipeline.
- **Poor self-rated state is rising.** Perceived mental health fair or
  poor rose `+13.9` pp/decade and perceived health fair or poor `+4.7`
  pp/decade; both are nonstationary.
- **Mental-health conditions are rising.** Anxiety (`+8.4` pp/decade) and
  mood disorders (`+5.5` pp/decade, break at 2020) both increased.
- **Some behaviours improve.** Daily smoking fell `-4.4` pp/decade, though
  the regime split at 2020 shows the decline flattening after 2020
  (`-7.3` before, `-1.0` after).
- **Two series are flat.** Diabetes (`+0.8`) and having a regular
  healthcare provider (`-2.1`) are labelled **stationary** over the
  window — no evidence of a trend beyond year-to-year noise.

Read together, the family is a picture of rising self-reported distress
and falling life evaluation over a decade, with the clearest breaks
coinciding with 2020. The pipeline dates those breaks; this page does not
claim they are caused by the pandemic.

## Caveats

- **Survey estimate.** Every series is self-reported on a national survey,
  carrying sampling error and a coefficient-of-variation release policy;
  some cells are suppressed or flagged. Plotted values are published point
  estimates.
- **Measurement, not only change.** The CCHS collection frame changed over
  2015–2024 and 2020–2021 collection was disrupted by the pandemic. A
  step in a series may be a step in the measurement. Direction of the
  breaks is dated, not attributed.
- **Short window.** Ten annual points is a short series; the
  stationarity test has limited power, which is why some series are
  labelled *undetermined* rather than stationary.
- **Self-report and definition drift.** "Percent" mixes reported
  behaviour, diagnosed conditions, and self-rated state; each has a
  different relationship to health, and a survey question that changes
  wording does not change meaninglessly.
- **No sub-provincial rows.** Provincial only; regional survey series are
  separate products.
- **Revisions.** Statistics Canada may revise estimates; the published
  files are regenerated from the source on each build.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run sohbc fetch statcan_health_indicators
uv run sohbc build
```

Every series publishes `data/published/<key>.csv`,
`data/published/<key>_trend.json`, and
`data/published/<key>_by_sex_trend.json`. The selection and definitions
are in `src/sohbc/indicators.py`; add or remove a series there and rebuild.
